What is Perl and what are its key features?

Perl is a high-level, general-purpose, interpreted, dynamic programming language known for:
- **Powerful regular expressions** — arguably the best regex support of any language
- **Text processing** — built for parsing and transforming text
- **CPAN** — one of the largest module ecosystems
- **Sigils** — variables prefixed with `$`, `@`, `%` indicating type

Always use `use strict; use warnings;` — they catch many common mistakes.

```perl
#!/usr/bin/perl
use strict;
use warnings;

print "Hello, World!\n";
printf("Hello, %s!\n", "Perl");
say "Hello with newline";   # say adds \n automatically

# Run:
perl hello.pl
perl -e "print 'Hello\n'"   # one-liner
```

What are the three variable types in Perl (scalar, array, hash) and how do sigils work?

```perl
use strict; use warnings;

# Scalar ($) — single value
my $name   = "Alice";
my $age    = 30;
my $pi     = 3.14159;
my $undef  = undef;    # undefined

# Array (@) — ordered list
my @arr    = (1, 2, 3, 4, 5);
my @words  = qw(one two three four);   # quote words

# Hash (%) — key-value pairs
my %user   = (name => "Alice", age => 30);
my %config = ("host" => "localhost", "port" => 8080);

# Sigil rules:
# $name      — scalar (single value)
# @arr       — whole array
# $arr[0]    — one element from array (scalar sigil!)
# @arr[0,2]  — array slice
# %hash      — whole hash
# $hash{key} — one value from hash (scalar sigil!)
# @hash{@keys} — hash slice

# String operations
length($name)           # 5
uc($name); lc($name)    # uppercase, lowercase
substr($name, 0, 3)     # "Ali"
index($name, "ice")     # 1
$name . " Smith"        # concatenation

# Repetition
my $line = "-" x 40;        # "----...----"
my @zeros = (0) x 5;        # (0,0,0,0,0)
```

How do Perl regular expressions work? Show the key operators and flags.

```perl
my $str = "Hello, World! 123";

# Match operator m//
if ($str =~ /World/) { print "Found!\n"; }

# Capture groups ($1, $2, ...)
if ($str =~ /(\w+),\s*(\w+)/) {
    print "$1, $2\n";   # Hello, World
}

# Flags
/pattern/i    # case-insensitive
/pattern/g    # global (all matches)
/pattern/m    # multiline
/pattern/x    # extended (allow whitespace and comments)

# Global match — collect all
my @matches = ($str =~ /\d+/g);   # ('123')
while ($str =~ /(\w+)/g) { print "$1\n"; }

# Substitution s///
(my $new = $str) =~ s/World/Perl/;     # copy then substitute
$str =~ s/\d+/NUM/g;                   # replace all
$str =~ s/(\w+)/uc($1)/ge;            # /e evaluates replacement as code

# tr (transliterate)
(my $copy = $str) =~ tr/a-z/A-Z/;    # uppercase
$str =~ tr/aeiou//d;                   # delete vowels
my $count = ($str =~ tr/l//);         # count 'l's

# Named captures
if ($date =~ /(?<year>\d{4})-(?<month>\d{2})-(?<day>\d{2})/) {
    print $+{year}, "-", $+{month}, "-", $+{day};
}
```
